review.summary: Phase 92 is a genuinely well-evidenced, source-bound documentation/tooling follow-up, and its central claims hold up under inspection. The 23-command gate in docs/checks/phase-92.json actually executed (every exit_code 0, timeout false), its command list matches tools/check_phase.py commands_for(92) exactly (lines 71-94) and the count matches scope_evidence.qualification_check_count=23, and its source_sha256 641cd284… equals the reviewed fingerprint supplied in the prompt and the fingerprint recorded in docs/checks/phase-92-private-material.json (produced 16:06:42, two minutes before the gate at 16:08:03, passed true, 0 selected-value matches, 0 new tenant occurrences). The new fail-closed control scripts/check-published-payload.py is real: it byte-compares 129 published files (all of crates/scm-sdk/src and examples, Cargo.toml.orig→crate manifest, README/LICENSE/NOTICE) against the retained crates.io 0.1.1 receipt, rejects added, removed, symlinked, duplicated, absolute, traversal and non-normalized paths, and requires the on-disk src+examples inventory to equal the published set; its deliberate gap (normalized Cargo.toml/Cargo.lock/.cargo_vcs_info.json) is genuinely covered by tools/live_evidence.py runtime_fingerprint (lines 99-110, enforced at 266), which is also in the gate. All five attempt-01 findings are concretely closed: fetch-depth: 0 at ci.yml:24 plus a real shallow-clone-then-unshallow reproduction (tools/test_ci.py:57-78) and a derived-phase guard (44-55); the nonterminal CI observation is now cited from phase-91 remote_ci, phase-92 scope_evidence, docs/CI.md:108-112 and docs/RELEASE.md:42-46 and is honestly labelled "running"/"waiting"; RELEASE.md:37-40 now separates gate 91 (published source) from gate 92 (current CI); missing published inputs raise ValueError with a regression test; and the receipt is cross-bound to both clean proofs and the remote tag (tools/test_g10_release.py:30-49). No SDK runtime input changed — the whole diff is workflow, docs, tooling and the regenerated response-defaults sidecar — and phase status honestly records status in_progress, claude_review pending and advancement waiting on the remote gate. What keeps it below 9 is that documentation accuracy is this phase's core deliverable and docs/CI.md still contradicts the gate it now documents: lines 131-136 and 145-148 state in the present tense that the phase gate invokes scripts/check-dependencies.py and that the security audit and cross checks run, while commands_for(92) contains no dependency, cross, package or Rust execution; line 10 still says the maintenance release "uses the source-bound Phase 91 gate; the workflow assertions in tools/test_ci.py track that invocation" when test_ci.py:377 pins --phase 92. Correspondingly ci.yml:61-69 still installs cargo-audit/cargo-deny, adds four cross targets and prepares the locked dependency graph that no gate-92 command consumes, and tools/test_ci.py:113-122 pins that dead preparation in place. The net effect is that ordinary CI no longer audits dependencies on any push while the CI document says it does — the same stale-current-gate defect class the previous review raised, left in a sibling section of the file this phase edited.

findings.description: docs/CI.md still describes dependency and platform coverage the current CI gate does not execute. Lines 131-136 state "The phase gate invokes scripts/check-dependencies.py; it refreshes and records official RustSec provenance, audits the complete Cargo lock with warnings denied, and checks all-feature license/source/ban policy", and lines 145-148 state "The security audit inventories dependencies across all targets" and "The cross checks compile the transport-independent feature set". The contracts job now runs only `tools/check_phase.py --phase 92 --verification-only` (.forgejo/workflows/ci.yml:73), and commands_for(92) (tools/check_phase.py:71-94) contains no scripts/check-dependencies.py, scripts/check-cross.py, scripts/check-package.py or scripts/check-rust.py invocation. The same document discloses the reduction correctly at line 104 ("The source-release compiler/package/oracle/security/platform executions remain in Phase 91"), so the file contradicts itself, and the stale statements are the security-relevant ones: after this change no push or pull request performs a RustSec advisory audit or license/ban policy check, and nothing in the repository says so. The documentation guard added for this finding class only asserts the substring "--phase 92" appears in docs/CI.md (tools/test_ci.py:55), so it cannot detect this.
findings.required_fix: Rewrite docs/CI.md:131-148 so the dependency-audit, security-audit and cross-check paragraphs are explicitly scoped to the Phase 8/91 source-release gates and state plainly that gate 92 performs no dependency, license, cross-target or compiler execution, and that advisory scanning therefore resumes only in the next qualification phase. Add an assertion in tools/test_ci.py that every `scripts/check-*.py` named as currently executed in docs/CI.md actually appears in commands_for(the phase number parsed from the workflow).

findings.description: The contracts-and-package job still installs cargo-audit 0.22.2 and cargo-deny 0.20.2 from source (lines 61-64), adds four cross-compilation standard libraries, and runs `cargo +1.99.0 fetch --locked` plus offline `cargo metadata` (lines 65-69), but no command in commands_for(92) consumes any of it: the only cargo-family tool gate 92 needs is rustfmt, used by tools/generate_models.py:1027-1031. These steps are now pure cost and supply-chain surface on every push, and tools/test_ci.py:113-122 (test_qualification_prepares_complete_locked_graph_before_offline_checks) actively pins the fetch→metadata→gate ordering, so the dead preparation is locked in by a passing test that no longer protects any executed check.
findings.required_fix: Either drop the cargo-audit/cargo-deny installs, the `rustup target add` line and the fetch/metadata preparation from the contracts job and relax tools/test_ci.py:113-122 to apply only when the CI-executed gate contains a cargo-consuming command, or restore scripts/check-dependencies.py to the gate so the installed tools are actually used.

findings.description: "The G10 0.1.1 maintenance release uses the source-bound Phase 91 gate; the workflow assertions in `tools/test_ci.py` track that invocation." is stale in both clauses as a statement of current configuration: .forgejo/workflows/ci.yml:73 runs --phase 92 and tools/test_ci.py:377 asserts `tools/check_phase.py --phase 92 --verification-only` in the workflow; no test asserts a phase-91 invocation there (tools/test_g10_release.py:51-57 pins the canonical hash of commands_for(91), not the workflow). This is the same defect the attempt-01 review raised for docs/RELEASE.md:37, which was fixed, while this instance near the top of the CI document was not.
findings.required_fix: Reword docs/CI.md:10-12 to say the 0.1.1 source was qualified with the Phase 91 gate and that CI now executes the post-publication Phase 92 gate, which tools/test_ci.py pins.

findings.description: The phase-92 gate omits several generated-artifact checks that cover contracts/ files which this phase is still free to change, and the declared scope reduction does not name them. docs/phase-status.json:2330 lists the reduction as "compiler/package/oracle/dependency/platform/live", but the gate also drops tools/verify_gateway_bindings.py --check, tools/model_fixtures.py --check, tools/verify_native_fixtures.py, tools/generate_constants.py --check and their unit suites (all present in commands_for(91), lines 109-126). contracts/native-gateway-bindings.json, contracts/native-fixtures/* and the model-fixture corpus are inside the reviewed source fingerprint but have no executed check in this gate, so drift in them would be caught only by human review, not by the gate or by CI.
findings.required_fix: Either add the four omitted contract/generator checks to commands_for(92) (they are offline and fast relative to the gate), or extend the scope_reduction text in docs/phase-status.json:2330 and docs/CI.md:104 to name the gateway-binding, native-fixture, model-fixture and constants ledgers as deliberately unverified in this phase.

findings.description: The gate's final command reads docs/checks/phase-92-private-material.json, and the published-payload command reads docs/checks/release-registry-0.1.1.json. The private-material receipt and docs/checks/phase-92.json are currently untracked working-tree files (the attempt-01 equivalents are staged, the attempt-02 ones are not), and scripts/check-private-material.py check_receipt raises on a missing path (OSError → "filesystem_read_failed", nonzero exit). If the follow-up commit omits the attempt-02 receipts, the remote gate this phase's advancement depends on fails at its last command for a bookkeeping reason rather than a source reason.
findings.required_fix: Include docs/checks/phase-92.json, docs/checks/phase-92-private-material.json, docs/checks/phase-92-published-payload.json and the attempt-02 review artifacts in the qualified follow-up commit before pushing, and confirm the pushed tree contains the exact receipt paths named in commands_for(92).

evidence: docs/checks/phase-92.json:1-512 — 23 executed commands, every exit_code 0 and timeout false, source_sha256 641cd2841601b5670c3ab563b674e6a19a5a33565d97b571fe8e6a01604f5293, source_unchanged true, passed true, checked_at 2026-10-18T16:08:03Z; the command list and order match tools/check_phase.py:71-94 exactly and the count equals docs/phase-status.json:2332 qualification_check_count 23.

scripts/check-published-payload.py:30-68 — byte-compares every non-normalized published row against crates/scm-sdk/{src,examples}, crates/scm-sdk/Cargo.toml (for Cargo.toml.orig) and root README/LICENSE/NOTICE; rejects absolute, '..', backslash, NUL, duplicate and non-normalized paths (38-40), symlinked files or parents (53-54), missing/unreadable inputs as ValueError (55-58), and requires the on-disk src+examples set to equal the published set (62-68). Executed output: {"publishedPayloadUnchanged": true, "matchedFiles": 129}; docs/checks/phase-92-published-payload.json records publishedSourceCommit 7efd1372806bd1969663993de3083d393b20cc62 and publishedArchiveSha256 8339891e…d154, matching docs/checks/release-registry-0.1.1.json:12-14.

tools/test_g10_release.py:58-98 — negative tests drive payload.verify against a temporary tree for content change, file removal (assertRaisesRegex "missing or unreadable"), added file, symlinked addition, five malformed receipts and five unsafe/duplicate paths; tools/test_g10_release.py:30-49 cross-binds the registry receipt's version, sourceCommit, archiveSha256 and every file row to both docs/checks/release-source-7efd1372…/release-package-{1.89.0,1.99.0}.json (requireClean true, effectiveDirty false) and to refs/tags/v0.1.1^{} in docs/checks/release-tag-v0.1.1.json:11.

tools/live_evidence.py:99-110 and 261-268 — runtime_fingerprint hashes root Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock, LICENSE, NOTICE, crates/scm-sdk/Cargo.toml and every file under src/ and examples/, and the live receipt check requires envelope["runtimeInputsSha256"] == runtime_fingerprint(root); `tools/live_evidence.py --check` ran in the gate and printed {"checked": true, "nativeMethodsVerified": 16, "observedMethods": 22}, so the metadata the payload guard deliberately skips is bound.

docs/checks/phase-92-private-material.json:4-17 — sourceSha256 equals the reviewed fingerprint 641cd284…, headCommit 7efd1372…, sourceUnchanged true, passed true, 1409 git-visible files, 0 credential matches, 0 published-source registration matches, newOrChangedFilesCount 0; checkedAt 16:06:42 precedes the gate's 16:08:03, and the gate's --check reported {"receiptFresh": true, "privateScanReexecuted": false}.

.forgejo/workflows/ci.yml:21-25 sets fetch-depth: 0 and persist-credentials: false; tools/test_ci.py:44-55 parses the gate phase out of the workflow, requires fetch-depth: 0 whenever commands_for(that phase) contains a commit-range git command, and requires "--phase 92" in both docs/CI.md and docs/RELEASE.md; tools/test_ci.py:57-78 creates a real repository, clones it --depth 1, asserts `git diff --check <base>..HEAD` fails, then unshallows and asserts it passes.

tools/response_defaults.py:37-48 verify_rust_additions binds each of the three additive APIs to a declaration regex in crates/scm-sdk/src/{config,validation}.rs and to an invocation in crates/scm-sdk/examples/response_defaults.rs, rejecting symlinked sources; tools/test_g10_release.py:100-125 asserts six independent rename mutations each raise ValueError; the executed `tools/response_defaults.py --check` printed {"defaultBindings": 23, "redTeamBindings": 8, "outsideRedTeamBindings": 15}, and the inventory embeds generatorSha256, so the tool change forced regeneration of contracts/response-defaults.json.

crates/scm-sdk/examples/response_defaults.rs:6-28 is a real offline assertion-bearing example: it builds RequestOptions::without_response_defaults(), asserts !response_defaults(), round-trips a Red Team TargetResponse under Mode::ResponseWithoutDefaults with exact serde equality to the input, and asserts the default policy still inserts ws_response_timeout 110 and basic_auth_location HEADER.

tools/test_ci.py:247-276 runs the real documentation guard against a temporary root whose development version (0.2.0) differs from the recorded publication version (0.1.1), asserts it passes without skipping, then asserts it fails for a "currently unpublished" README and for a STABILITY.md missing its registry reference; tools/test_ci.py:278-301 performs the version-independent assertions before the receipt-specific early return, and with the real repository at 0.1.1 it asserts CHANGELOG.md contains the archive SHA-256, source commit and publication date (present at CHANGELOG.md:3-8).

Honest status recording: docs/checks/release-ci-0.1.1-observation-01.json:5-29 records runs 16/17 as "running"/"waiting" with the limitation "waiting/running is not a passing CI result"; docs/phase-status.json:2294-2310 mirrors that as remote_ci "observed_nonterminal"; docs/phase-status.json:2315, 2336, 2346 and 2423-2427 keep phase 92 in_progress with claude_review pending and advancement conditioned on the remote gate; docs/VALIDATION.md:38-42 states the 27,216-case typed corpus was not replayed under ResponseWithoutDefaults.

Contradicting current-gate prose: docs/CI.md:132-136 ("The phase gate invokes scripts/check-dependencies.py…"), docs/CI.md:145-148 ("The security audit inventories dependencies across all targets… The cross checks compile…") and docs/CI.md:10-12 ("uses the source-bound Phase 91 gate; the workflow assertions in tools/test_ci.py track that invocation") against tools/check_phase.py:71-94, which contains no dependency, cross, package or Rust command, and tools/test_ci.py:377, which pins --phase 92.

Scope confinement verified: the modified/added set is .forgejo/workflows/ci.yml, CHANGELOG.md, contracts/response-defaults.json, docs/{CI,PHASES,RELEASE,VALIDATION,g10-0.1.1-plan,phase-status}.md/json, scripts/check-published-payload.py, tools/{check_phase,response_defaults,test_ci,test_g10_release}.py plus docs/checks and docs/reviews receipts — no crates/scm-sdk source, example, manifest, README or legal file, consistent with the payload guard's 129 matched files.
limitations: Read-only Read/Glob/Grep only: I could not execute git, the phase gate, Python, Rust or CI, so every pass/fail statement about commands rests on the recorded receipts plus static reading of the scripts.

I cannot compute SHA-256 with the available tools, so I could not independently confirm that docs/checks/phase-92.json hashes to 270bdd77e6d497859e521b062075a80255733069a324885fab7cf264fd7dbffc, nor recompute tools/review_phase.py fingerprint() over the worktree; I verified only that the receipt's recorded source_sha256 equals the fingerprint quoted in the prompt and in the private-material receipt.

docs/checks/ and docs/reviews/ are excluded from the review fingerprint (tools/review_phase.py:13), so the registry, tag, clean-package and CI-observation receipts are not hashed into the reviewed source. tools/test_g10_release.py now pins the commit and archive digest as literals in hashed source and cross-checks the proofs and tag, but nothing re-derives the archive digest from the file rows, so a coordinated edit of receipt plus proofs plus working tree would still pass; this rests on the repository-writer trust assumption stated in docs/PHASES.md:7.

I did not open any credential or tenant-registration file, so the private-material scan's selected-value coverage is accepted from its sanitized receipt and from the recorded tools/test_auxiliary_evidence.py results rather than re-derived.

Registry, remote tag and remote CI facts come entirely from retained receipts; I made no network call to crates.io or the Forgejo instance, so the current state of the published crate, the tag and runs 16/17 as of this review is unverified.

Compiler, package, oracle, dependency, cross-target and live-service behaviour were not re-executed in this phase by design; I assessed whether the stated scope reduction is justified by proven byte-identity with the published archive rather than re-establishing that evidence.
The claim that the updated workflow passes remotely is untested by anyone: no run of the fetch-depth: 0 / gate-92 configuration exists yet, and the phase itself defers advancement until one does.
